data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Starting from any known 45-comparator 13-input sorting network, no single-comparator removal preserves the 0-1 property (i.e., the network still sorts all 8192 binary vectors). This means the 45-to-44 transition requires at least two simultaneous structural changes, explaining why local search and incremental pruning stall at 45.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If any single comparator can be removed from any known 45-comparator n=13 network while maintaining the 0-1 sorting property, the local-minimum claim is falsified and the barrier is not structural.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a sequence of local moves (single comparator additions, removals, or endpoint swaps, each step maintaining the 0-1 property) leads from a 45-comparator network to a 44-comparator network, the disconnection claim is falsified.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 45-comparator network used as the starting point is later shown to contain redundant comparators (comparators whose removal does not affect sorting), the premise that all 45 are load-bearing is falsified.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A 45-comparator network is a fixed sequence of 45 comparator pairs (i,j) with 0\u2264i<j<13. For each of the 45 comparators, we test removal: delete that comparator, keep the other 44, and run all 2^13=8192 binary vectors through the resulting 44-comparator network. If every single-removal fails the 0-1 test, then the 45-comparator network is a local minimum under the 'remove one comparator' move. This implies 44-comparator networks (if they exist) are structurally distant\u2014they cannot be reached by greedily trimming comparators from a known 45, and search must instead find them via a different construction path (e.g., a novel global structure or a multi-step replacement chain where intermediate states are not themselves valid sorting networks).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
